item.research_question: What are the mechanisms of fatigue crack initiation and propagation in high-entropy alloys?
item.material_system: High-entropy alloys, including CrCoFeMnNi, Al0.5CoCrFeNi, and Al0.7CoCrFeNi
item.test_conditions: Cyclic loading, rotating bending fatigue test, and tensile test at room temperature and low temperature
key_findings: Slip is one of the main mechanisms of crack initiation in high-entropy alloys
The presence of high-entropy configurations leads to a higher likelihood of dislocation formation along parallel slip planes
The fatigue performance of high-entropy alloys is significantly influenced by both inherent defects within the alloy and defects introduced during processing
The introduction of a multi-component B2 phase with ductility and transformability into high-entropy alloys can improve fatigue life
The combination of ultrafine grain and transformation-induced plasticity (TRIP) can increase fatigue resistance
item.mechanism: The authors propose that the mechanisms of fatigue crack initiation and propagation in high-entropy alloys are related to slip, dislocation formation, and the presence of defects
item.limitations: The authors note that the study of fatigue behavior in high-entropy alloys is still in its early stages and more research is needed to fully understand the mechanisms
item.future_work: The authors propose that future research should focus on systematically studying the fatigue strength of high-entropy alloys under various loading conditions and investigating the effect of environmental conditions on fatigue performance
quotes: Slip is one of the main mechanisms of crack initiation in the CrCoFeMnNi alloy
The presence of high-entropy configurations leads to a higher likelihood of dislocation formation along parallel slip planes
The fatigue performance of high-entropy alloys is significantly influenced by both inherent defects within the alloy and defects introduced during processing

System: High-entropy alloys, including CrCoFeMnNi, Al0.5CoCrFeNi, and Al0.7CoCrFeNi. Test conditions: Cyclic loading, rotating bending fatigue test, and tensile test at room temperature and low temperature. Findings: Slip is one of the main mechanisms of crack initiation in high-entropy alloys; The presence of high-entropy configurations leads to a higher likelihood of dislocation formation along parallel slip planes; The fatigue performance of high-entropy alloys is significantly influenced by both inherent defects within the alloy and defects introduced during processing; The introduction of a multi-component B2 phase with ductility and transformability into high-entropy alloys can improve fatigue life; The combination of ultrafine grain and transformation-induced plasticity (TRIP) can increase fatigue resistance.
